Studio Lite uses Roblox’s Cloud API Keys to publish your game to a starter place on your profile.
1)  In the Roblox mobile app, tap the “More (…)” icon at the bottom of the screen.
2)  Tap the “Create (</>)” icon. (Or the Create tab if you're on a browser.)
3)  If you don’t see “Open Cloud” in the menu on the left, tap “☰” near Home or Creator Hub.
4)  Tap “Open Cloud”, then “API Keys”, then “Create API Key”.
5)  In “(1) General Information” enter a name for your key.  For example, type “key”.
6)  In “(2) Access Permissions” select API system: “universe-places”, then tap “Add API System”.
7)  Select your starter Experience (like “yourname’s Place”).  Then tap “Add Experience”.
8)  Select “write” from the “Experience Operations” drop-down list. (Result: "universe-places:write").
9)  Repeat steps 6 through 8 above except this time in step 6 select API System “universe”.  And, in step 8 choose both "write" operations. (Result: "universe.place:write" and "universe:write").
10)  In “(3) Security” enter “0.0.0.0/0” and tap “Add IP Address”.

Be sure to Teleport to your game from Studio Lite’s Published page (in the Splash menu).  Then you can find your game easily in the future in the Roblox “Continue” menu.  While playing your game, be sure to use the Invite feature in the Roblox icon.

11)  Tap “Save & Generate Key”.  The api-key is a long string of letters and numbers.  You must tap “Copy Key To Clipboard”, paste it into Studio Lite’s “Publish” page.  If you lose it, you can “Edit” your key and “regenerate” a new api-key to copy.
Then tap “☰” near Dashboard and choose “Places”, then tap your place’s icon (you might have to tap it twice) to get to the Basic Settings page.
Now you can press “☰” again to see choices for icon, thumbnails, etc.  Game names, descriptions and images are moderated by Roblox, so there might be a delay before they become visible.

To update your Experience’s icon and thumbnails use the Roblox Creator Hub:  From the Roblox mobile App, tap “More (…)”, then tap “Create (</>)”.  Then tap on your experience (like “yourname’s Place”) then choose “Manage Experience”.
Changes made in the Roblox Creator Hub will cause your game to be removed from Studio Lite’s Published list.  If you want it back on the list, publish it again.

LocalScripts run on your device and their actions are usually not seen by the server or by other players unless it remote calls a Server Event.  Studio Lite automatically inserts a prewritten LocalScript when you insert a server Script that needs a remote call.  The GuiHideLocal is a handy way to close a Gui when the player is done reading it, if no server interaction is needed.  If the server does need to act on the click, insert the Script (not localscript): GuiActivatedScript.  It will automatically insert a child LocalScript to activate the button.

The blue localscripts are remote called from server script or they call a remote server script.  The word "Remote" is used to remind us that the localscript is running on your device, which is usually miles away from the server running the server script.

This localscript is remote called from server scripts to create, update or delete something on the client side.
It is most often used to show or update Guis on the client, but can be used to modify other types of Instances. This localscript is already inserted into StarterPlayer.StarterCharacterScripts.  Find it in the Explorer window on the right and open it for more details.

This localscript is automatically included when you insert the server script: ToolScript.  It remote calls the ToolScript passing the mouse click (or screen tap) position to the ToolScript.  This is handy for tools that shoot at or point at objects in the Workspace.

This localscript is typically placed inside a Close or Exit TextButton with text set to a red X.  The button usually goes in the top-right corner of a Frame.  This localscript hides the Gui frame when the button is clicked/tapped.
Blank LocalScript.  Reminder: Changes made to object in LocalScript are not typically seen by other players.

Scripts are written in the Lua programming language.  They tell the server to perform some actions, like move parts, change properties, create/destroy parts, update leaderboards, etc.  Studio Lite provides some common scripts already typed for you.  Or, you can type your own.
The blue scripts below are Read-Only.  You can change child values to customize their behavior.
The green scripts are examples prewritten in the Roblox Lua programming language.  You are free to edit them as you wish.

Insert this script inside an anchored part to make it move back and forth. Edit variables in the script to adjust the speed and distance. This can be used to push players off a platform, or as a moving obstacle.
This script lets you change any object property values and clone/destroy objects, when the parent PlayerGui Button is mouse-clicked or screen-tapped by a player.

Insert this script inside an anchored part to make it circle by continually adding small movements and rotations to the part's current position. This can be used to push players, or as a moving obstacle.

Respawn/Destroy the parent model/part if it moves too far, stops moving too long, or if an NPC that dies.  Can be used to spawn a new car when the previous car is driven away. And cleanup/destroy abandoned cars.

Insert this script into a part to continuously change that part's properties over time.  You can change Transparency, CanCollide, Color, Size and CFrame. Make a door or platform periodically become non-collidable or invisible or both.

When a player touches this script's parent part, a Gui text message you previously created will be visible and optionally hide it after a few seconds.  Useful to show "Success", or give the player a new quest.
This script demostrates how to make an explosion when a player touches a part.  An explosion will automatically detonate when place in the Workspace.  Then it automatically destroys itself.
Insert a tool (or accessory, hair, hat, etc) into the player's character.  The tool is cloned from the path you specify (usually from ServerStorage).
Remove a tool (or accessory, hair, hat, etc) from the player's character and backpack.
This script lets you change any object property values and clone/destroy objects, when the parent part is touched by a player.
When the player touches this script's parent, the player becomes a ghost!  And then changes back after 8 seconds.
When this script's parent part is touched, the player will either lose health or gain health by the amount you put in the script.
When this script's parent part is touched, update some leaderboard stats.  For example, if a coin is touched, play a Sound, update Coins leaderstats, and hide the coin for a few seconds.
When this script's parent part is touched, the player will be teleported to the location you choose.
Place this script in ServerScriptService to update a datastore with all players' leaderstats, Inventory, and playerstats as they change (after a 5 seccond delay).
This script lets you build your own tool.  A child local script captures the player's click location and passes it to this server script.  Insert this inside a Tool object.
This script runs your code when a player joins and/or character spawns.  Typically this would go inside the ServerScriptsService folder.

You can change any object property and clone/destroy objects with loops and 'if' conditions.  Place in ServerScriptService to make a game loop or reward players with a coin every minute.  Place in a model to destroy or explode after a wait time.
This script lets you change any object property values and clone/destroy objects, when the parent Part or model is mouse-clicked or screen-tapped by a player.
Place this script into ServerScriptService to convert all players to R6.
Animating in a place with scripts or moving parts may make unwanted changes to your place. Script(s) have been detected in this place.
Your root part is not anchored. This may lead to weird behavior. Want us to anchor it for you?
Add script to rig to play this animation.
QUICK START:  Tap a number in the timeline in the top row to move the blue box.  Then, tap a body part in the list on the left.
Now you can Rotate the body part, and test it using the Play button (▶) on the left. If you want to Move instead of Rotate, tap the word "Rotate" in the top bar.
You can tap or drag keyframes (Kf) to copy or move them. Tap a green pose to copy it. Use the EDIT menu to paste or adjust your animation looping and length.
SAVE YOUR WORK:  Tap ANIM, Save to overwrite or create a new KeyframeSequence. You MUST ALSO SAVE YOUR STUDIO LITE GAME!
Currently, Roblox security prevents uploading an Animation ID to your account.
When you Save your animation, checkmark the "Add Script to rig..." to install the script.
To get the animation ID of an Emote, use the Toolbox model importer with the emote's asset id, then look at its properties.
You can also find some KeyframeSequences in models at create.roblox.com/models . Search for ANIMSAVES.
But, Studio Lite can play KeyframeSequences in Play/test mode and in your Published game using a script called AnimationLitePlayScript.
IMPORT ANIMATIONS:  You can import public animations using Studio Lite's Toolbox Model importer. Just paste the animation ID.
Or you can copy the code into a tool equipped or activated script to trigger it.
If your animation doesn't blend well with Roblox animations, you can disable Roblox's Animate script in the rig.
The script has comments and examples that can help you stop your animation early, or pause you script until the animation is done.

--AnimationLiteService - Adapted verious examples to create a Procedural KeyframeSequence player using C0 so it blends with regular animations. ScottSpiritWalker, 08/21/2025. local TS = game:GetService("TweenService") local runservice = game:GetService("RunService") local tStyle, tDirection = { [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.Linear] = Enum.EasingStyle.Linear; [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.Bounce] = Enum.EasingStyle.Bounce; [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.Cubic] = Enum.EasingStyle.Cubic; [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.CubicV2] = Enum.EasingStyle.Cubic; [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.Elastic] = Enum.EasingStyle.Elastic; [Enum.PoseEasingStyle.Constant] = Enum.EasingStyle.Linear; },{ [Enum.PoseEasingDirection.In] = Enum.EasingDirection.In; [Enum.PoseEasingDirection.Out] = Enum.EasingDirection.Out; [Enum.PoseEasingDirection.InOut]= Enum.EasingDirection.InOut; } function PlayKeyframeSequence(Model, KeyframeSequence, SpeedMult, StartAtFrameNum, StopAtFrameNum) if not Model or not Model.Parent

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -- AnimationLitePlayScript -- This Script is automatically inserted into a Rig by -- -- Studio Lite's "Animation Lite" if checkmarked while saving the KeyframeSequence. -- -- You are free to change this script, place it inside Players, trigger it by GUI -- -- or play it when a part is touched or a tool is equipped. Be sure to change the -- -- script name so the checkmark in Animation Lite won't overwrite your work. -- -- --ScottSpiritWalker, 10/30/2025. -- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- local AnimationLitePlayEvent = game.ServerScriptService.AnimationLiteService.AnimationLitePlayEvent task.wait(1) --wait for server to start so you can see the animation. AnimationLitePlayEvent:Fire(script.Parent, script.KeyframeSequence.Value,1) --Start playing animation and continue this script. ...[truncated]
